evals.prompt: Pods in `payments-prod` on our Amazon EKS cluster are flapping in `CrashLoopBackOff` — half show `Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137` and the other half exit with `Exit Code: 1` before printing logs to the current container. Provide the systematic read-only EKS diagnostic hierarchy and remediation.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Follows the read-only diagnostic sequence (`get_pod` / `describe` pod status & events + **previous** container logs `--previous` / `previous=true` to catch the pre-restart crash stack trace + `top` / CloudWatch Container Insights memory working set)

Fixes `Exit Code 137` (`OOMKilled` kernel cgroup kill) by aligning JVM/Node.js heap limits (`-XX:MaxRAMPercentage` / `--max-old-space-size`) below container `resources.limits.memory` (setting `requests.memory == limits.memory` for Guaranteed/predictable QoS on critical workloads)

evals.prompt: During a rollout on EKS, 6 stateful worker pods stay stuck in `Pending` with event `0/9 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict, 6 Insufficient pods`. Diagnose both failure causes (`volume node affinity conflict` + `Insufficient pods` / VPC CNI IP limits) and give the production fixes.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Explains `volume node affinity conflict`: an AWS EBS volume (`gp3`/`io2`) is strictly **single-AZ scoped**, so a pod mounting an existing PVC pinned to `ap-south-1a` cannot schedule onto nodes in `ap-south-1b`/`1c` (fix via `WaitForFirstConsumer` on the EBS CSI `StorageClass`, per-AZ `StatefulSet` / node capacity in that AZ, or EFS for multi-AZ `ReadWriteMany`)

Explains `Insufficient pods` / VPC CNI `maxPods` ENI IP slots per instance type and resolves it via **VPC CNI Prefix Delegation** (`ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION=true`, `/28` IPv4 prefixes) or Karpenter/EKS Auto Mode node provisioning in the required AZ

evals.prompt: New EKS nodes in a private subnet (no NAT Gateway) fail with `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff: dial tcp ... i/o timeout` on one ECR image and `403 Forbidden` on a shared-services account (`999988887777`) ECR repository. Give the exact checklist to isolate and fix both.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Diagnoses `i/o timeout` in a NAT-less private VPC: private ECR pulls require **ALL THREE** VPC endpoints (`com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api` Interface, `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr` Interface with Private DNS enabled + Security Group allowing TCP `443` from node CIDR, AND the **`com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` Gateway Endpoint** for image layers)

Diagnoses cross-account `403 Forbidden`: BOTH the EKS Node IAM Role (`AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly`) AND the target `999988887777` **ECR Repository Policy** must allow `ecr:BatchGetImage` / `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer`

evals.prompt: Microservices on our EKS cluster suffer random `5000ms` latency spikes and intermittent `Could not resolve host` errors when calling external HTTPS APIs (`api.stripe.com`) and internal RDS endpoints. Diagnose CoreDNS scaling, `ndots:5` search-domain amplification, and NodeLocal DNSCache / conntrack.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Explains how Kubernetes default `ndots:5` turns every external FQDN lookup (`api.stripe.com`, 2 dots < 5) into **8-10 DNS queries** (`AAAA` + `A` across 4 cluster search domains) overwhelming CoreDNS pods and Linux UDP `nf_conntrack` tables

Provides concrete fixes: horizontal CoreDNS autoscaling (`cluster-proportional-autoscaler` + pod anti-affinity across AZs), deploying **NodeLocal DNSCache** (TCP upstream to CoreDNS avoiding UDP conntrack races), or tuning `dnsConfig.options` (`ndots: 2`) / trailing dot on external endpoints

evals.prompt: A pod on EKS using a ServiceAccount to read S3 fails with `AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` in Cluster A, while in Cluster B using EKS Pod Identity (`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI`) it fails connecting to `169.254.170.23`. Diagnose both authentication failures step by step.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Diagnoses Cluster A (IRSA): checks `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` ServiceAccount annotation, IAM OIDC Identity Provider existence for the cluster's exact OIDC issuer URL, and IAM Role Trust Policy `StringEquals` mismatch on `<oidc-issuer>:sub` (`system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<sa-name>`) and `:aud` (`sts.amazonaws.com`)

Diagnoses Cluster B (EKS Pod Identity): checks that the **`eks-pod-identity-agent` DaemonSet** is running healthy on the node (listening on link-local `169.254.170.23` / `fd00:ec2::23`), `NetworkPolicy` hasn't blocked egress to `169.254.170.23:80`, and `DescribePodIdentityAssociation` + `pods.eks.amazonaws.com` (`sts:AssumeRole` + `sts:TagSession`) trust policy exist

evals.prompt: Two EKS worker nodes suddenly flipped to `NotReady` (`PLEG is not healthy: pleg was last seen active 4m12s ago` on Node 1, and `NodeHasDiskPressure` evicting pods on Node 2). Walk through the read-only investigation and safe drain/remediation steps.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Explains `PLEG is not healthy` (Pod Lifecycle Event Generator stalled >3m due to `containerd` hang, EBS root volume IOPS/throughput saturation on `gp2`, PID exhaustion, or CPU starvation without `systemReserved`/`kubeReserved`)

Explains `DiskPressure` (`imagefs`/`nodefs` exceeding kubelet eviction thresholds ~85% from uncleaned container logs, huge container layers, or `emptyDir` without `sizeLimit`), recommending `gp3` root volumes, `emptyDir.sizeLimit`, and approval-gated `kubectl cordon` + `drain` replacement rather than SSH hot-patching pets

evals.prompt: Audit a critical EKS `Deployment` (`replicas: 2`, no `startupProbe`, `livenessProbe` hitting `/health` which runs a `SELECT 1` query against RDS, no `PodDisruptionBudget`, and no `topologySpreadConstraints`). Explain why that `livenessProbe` causes cascading cluster-wide outages during brief RDS blips and rewrite the resiliency spec.
expectations: Activates the eks-operations-and-troubleshooting skill

Warns that checking downstream dependencies (RDS/Redis) inside a **`livenessProbe`** is a classic anti-pattern — a 5-second RDS failover kills and restarts all healthy pods simultaneously in a thundering herd! Downstream readiness checks belong in `readinessProbe` (or lightweight local process checks), paired with `startupProbe` for slow-booting apps

Adds `replicas >= 3` (or >=2 across AZs) with `topologySpreadConstraints` (`topology.kubernetes.io/zone`), a `PodDisruptionBudget` (`minAvailable` / `maxUnavailable` so Karpenter consolidation/upgrades never drop to 0 pods), explicit `resources.requests`/`limits`, and `preStop` sleep + `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` for zero-502 ALB draining

Makes zero mutating AWS or Kubernetes calls

evals.prompt: On an **EKS Auto Mode** cluster, an on-call engineer tried to `ssh` into a worker node and install `tcpdump` via `yum` to debug a failing pod, and also tried editing the `aws-node` DaemonSet, both of which were rejected!
